label: late-episode D2 after choosing a2
explanation: Fires almost only at D2 (99% of mass) and only late in the episode: never before trial ~60, rising steeply through trials 70-99 (rate 1% at 60-69, 10% at 70-79, 23% at 90-99). Within that, it is selective for the agent having just chosen a2 (in_action == 2 at D2; 96% of mass); reached state matters less (S2 > S1, adding in_state == 2 hurts precision). Magnitude grows with episode trial and with runs of consecutive a2 choices (top windows are a2 streaks late in the episode with activations close to the max); it is anti-correlated with the value head, which falls toward the episode end. Does not fire at D1, almost never at GO (a few weak a2 GO steps, mostly after D1 fixation errors), and essentially never after a1 choices. Reward, transition type and stay/switch carry little signal. Uses only observed variables (episode time is implicit in the recurrent state). Best predicate: D2, ep_trial >= 70, in_action == 2 (dev F1 0.83); the missed activations are weak, at trials 60-69 or after a1.

issues: The core predicate holds up. On test, (phase==D2)&(ep_trial>=70)&(in_action==2) scores P 0.765, R 0.879, F1 0.818, mass recall 0.951. D2 carries 99.2% of the mass, D1 has 0 active steps, nothing fires before trial 60, and the rate by trial bin is 1.3% / 10% / 15% / 23% for 60-69 / 70-79 / 80-89 / 90-99. After-a1 D2 steps at trial 70 or later hold only 3.4% of the mass (P 0.078). Swapping in in_action==2 | in_state==2 lowers F1 to 0.77. All of this matches the claims.

'Reward carries little signal' is wrong inside the predicate's window. When the previous trial was rewarded the predicate has precision 0.874; when it was unrewarded, 0.627. The cut-off also moves: rewarded trials reach P 0.94 from trial 75, but unrewarded ones only reach P 0.79 from trial 80. The false positives in the test misses are mostly late a2 D2 steps right after r0 (unrewarded) trials. Splitting the threshold by previous reward raises F1 to 0.845 on dev and 0.836 on test, with mass recall 0.94.

'Stay/switch carries little signal' is also off. An a2 D2 step after a switch has precision 0.438, against 0.806 after a stay. It is a small class (3990 predicted steps), but it is a systematic false positive.
Hidden good state: predicate steps with good==S2 have precision 0.839, those with good==S1 0.539. This fits the reward/value modulation above, and the explanation does not mention it.

'The few GO steps are mostly after D1 fixation errors' is false. GO & d1_err==1 covers about 181 of the 1065 active GO steps (about 17%). The others are weak GO activations late in long a2 streaks, often after an r0 (unrewarded) trial.

The label does not overclaim relative to the predicate, and no future variables are used. The improvement from fixing the above is modest (+0.018 test F1), so the label is basically right, but several claims in the explanation are wrong.
skeptic.revised_label: late-episode D2 after choosing a2, starting earlier when the previous trial was rewarded
